                                            PROJECT NO. 58481

    RULEMAKING TO IMPLEMENT                               §        PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
    LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION                            §
    STANDARDS UNDER PURA § 37.0561                        §                 OF TEXAS

             GUADALUPE VALLEY ELECTRIC COOPERATIVE, INC.’S (GVEC)
                 COMMENTS ON THE PROPOSAL FOR PUBLICATION

           Guadalupe Valley Electric Cooperative, Inc. (GVEC) respectfully submits these comments

in response to the proposal for publication (PFP) regarding large load interconnection standards

(LLIS).1 GVEC is a member-owned Texas electric cooperative with transmission and distribution

assets that provides retail electric service to its members in its statutorily authorized service area.

GVEC operates as both a Distribution Service Provider (DSP) and, where it owns transmission-

level facilities, a Transmission Service Provider (TSP) within its service territory, and so it is

directly and substantially affected by the proposed rule. The PFP directed comments to be filed by

April 17; accordingly, these comments are timely.

                                                I.       Comments

           GVEC supports the Commission’s efforts to implement PURA § 37.0561 and establish a

formal framework for large load interconnections. GVEC urges the Commission to make a few

fundamental improvements before adoption: first, the rule must clearly and consistently delineate

the respective roles and responsibilities of the DSP and the TSP at every stage of the

interconnection process, with the DSP serving as the customer’s primary point of contact. The

current draft leaves some of this to each negotiated agreement, which will produce inconsistent

outcomes, disputes and administrative burden across the ERCOT footprint. Second, the

Commission should adopt a standardized agreement framework analogous to the Standard



1
    Proposal for Publication of New 16 TAC §25.194 (Mar. 12, 2026) (PFP).


                                                                                                     1
 Generator Interconnection Agreement (SGIA) used for generator interconnections, rather than

merely establishing minimum requirements that each utility must independently implement.

ERCOT’s Planning Guide and pending Planning Guide Revisions Requests (PGRRs) address only

the TSP-to-ERCOT study interface, not the customer-facing agreements this rule requires.

           So as not to burden the Commission with repetitive comments, GVEC also supports and

incorporates by reference the comments of Texas Electric Cooperatives, Inc. regarding the

§ 25.194(b)(3) applicability trigger, curtailment authority for loads exceeding contracted peak

demand, the contribution in aid of construction (CIAC) exemption for electric cooperatives and

MOUs under PURA § 35.004(c-2), the rate base offset concerns, study responsibility demarcation,

letter of credit form acceptance, financial security timing, and the request for further comment

opportunity if the PFP changes substantially.

               1. The DSP Must Serve as the Large Load Customer’s Primary Interface

           The DSP’s primacy in the customer relationship is not a policy preference, it is a

requirement of Texas utility law. Under PURA, the DSP is the only entity holding a certificate of

convenience and necessity to provide retail electric delivery service.2 The customer’s legal service

relationship runs entirely through the DSP and the customer has no direct service relationship with

the TSP. The proposed rule is not clear enough on this point. Although the rule language implies

that the DSP will have primary responsibility because it introduces the interconnecting TSP as a

signatory to the agreements only when the TSP is different than the interconnecting DSP, it never

overtly says which entity serves the customer, and it leaves allocation of the entities’

responsibilities to the negotiated intermediate and interconnection agreements.




2
    Tex. Util. Code § 37.051.


                                                                                                  2
          Clarity on this point is especially important to GVEC, because as an electric cooperative

and a non-opt-in entity (NOIE) it has an obligation to provide not only distribution services, but

also retail power supply to its customers. In some parts of its service territory, GVEC owns

transmission facilities ≤138 kV voltage, but all higher voltage transmission facilities within its

service territory are owned and operated by other TSPs. For interconnections where new

substations and transformers will be required, GVEC may or may not be the TSP who builds and

owns those facilities.3 To date, there has been confusion for new customers about which entity to

contact when they are seeking to interconnect a new large load. In some cases, potential customers

have contacted a TSP directly, and GVEC did not know about the new customer until work has

already been performed by the TSP to study the load.

         GVEC urges the Commission to establish a clear functional split on the face of the rule that

controls interpretation of responsibilities. The DSP must serve as the large load customer’s primary

point of contact for executing and administering the Intermediate and Interconnection agreements.

The DSP should receive distribution-level CIAC and administer true-ups for distribution-level

facilities. The DSP will provide retail delivery service, operational coordination, and billing of

transmission and distribution costs. The DSP will bear responsibility for load shed obligations,

emergency curtailments and distribution-level reliability. The TSP must coordinate with ERCOT

to initiate and monitor the interconnection study and remit ERCOT’s study costs on behalf of the

large load customer. The TSP should receive and hold financial security posted by the large load

customer for transmission equipment and upgrades.4 The TSP should receive the non-refundable



3
  PURA § 35.056 spells out the rights of TSPs to build and own new transmission facilities, and in some cases new
transmission facilities will be owned and operated by other TSPs, even if the new large load is GVEC’s retail
customer.
4
  It may be appropriate for the DSP to act as an intermediary between the large load customer and the TSP with
respect to financial security, but the financial obligation should belong with the customer, and the beneficiary should
be the TSP for monies that secure payment for transmission facilities or ERCOT studies.


                                                                                                                     3
 interconnection fee and handle the resulting offset or credit to transmission rates. The TSP should

receive transmission-level CIAC and administer true-ups for transmission-level facilities. The TSP

should notify ERCOT of withdrawals, amendments, and non-utilized transmission capacity.

          These divisions of responsibility mirror the existing functional boundary between

ERCOT’s protocols, which focus on communications with Transmission Operators, and the retail

service framework, which is between customers and DSPs. Section (f)(7)(B) of the PFP already

assigns the non-refundable interconnection fee specifically to the TSP. GVEC recommends that

the Commission add this same level of specificity to the rule for each responsibility instead of

repeatedly using the phrase “interconnecting DSP or interconnecting TSP.”

               2. The Commission Should Create Standard Agreement Forms

          GVEC recommends that the Commission use this proceeding to create standard forms for

the Intermediate and Interconnection agreements with large loads. None of ERCOT’s approved

Planning Guides or proposed Planning Guide Revision Requests (PGRRs) contemplate, propose,

or would authorize a standard-form agreement between large loads and interconnecting DSPs and

TSPs. The Commission should approve a standard agreement form similar to the Standard

Generation Interconnection Agreement (SGIA) that the Commission’s rules require generators to

sign before they can interconnect with the ERCOT grid.5 As with the SGIA, a standard agreement

in the large load context should allow the parties to tailor the agreements by mutual agreement to

address specific facts presented by the particular interconnection so long as the changes are not

otherwise inconsistent with this rule.

          If the Commission does not adopt standard forms in this rulemaking, or at a minimum

direct their development on a defined timeline, each DSP and TSP across the ERCOT footprint



5
    See 16 Tex. Admin. Code § 25.195.


                                                                                                 4
 will develop its own agreements, producing inconsistent terms and enforcement mechanisms,

confusion and transaction costs for large load customers who must evaluate materially different

agreements across multiple utilities, and potential disputes about whether a given utility’s form

satisfies the requirements of this rule.

        Consistent with GVEC’s comments above, the form agreements should clearly define the

responsibilities of each party.

                                           II.   Conclusion

        GVEC appreciates the opportunity to provide these comments and respectfully urges the

Commission to clarify the roles and responsibilities of the DSP and TSP consistently throughout

the rule and develop or direct the development of a Commission-approved standard form

Intermediate Agreement and Interconnection Agreement for Large Loads.

Dated: April 17, 2026


                                                    Respectfully submitted,




                                                    Amanda Frazier
                                                    State Bar No. 24032198
                                                    General Counsel & Chief Regulatory
                                                    Officer, GVEC
                                                    P.O. Box 118
                                                    Gonzales, Texas 78629
                                                    (210) 945-5039
                                                    afrazier@gvec.org

                                      PROJECT NO. 58481

 RULEMAKING TO IMPLEMENT                         §         PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
 LARGE LOAD INTERCONNECTION                      §
 STANDARDS UNDER PURA § 37.0561                  §                    OF TEXAS

              EXECUTIVE SUMMARY OF GVEC’S COMMENTS ON THE PFP

       GVEC supports the Public Utility Commission’s proposal to implement LLIS under PURA

§ 37.0561 but urges several key changes before adoption to ensure clarity, consistency, and

efficiency.

       Clarify DSP vs. TSP roles - The rule should clearly and consistently define the

responsibilities of DSPs and TSPs at every stage of the large load interconnection process. The

DSP should be the large load customer’s primary point of contact, since Texas law establishes that

the customer’s retail service relationship exists only with the DSP, not the TSP. Leaving role

allocation to negotiated agreements will lead to inconsistency and potential disputes. Clear

assignments will reduce customer confusion and prevent duplicative or misaligned actions.

       Adopt standard agreement forms - GVEC strongly recommends that the Commission

create Commission-approved standard forms for the Intermediate and Interconnection Agreements

for large loads similar to the SGIA used for generators.

       Support for Texas Electric Cooperative, Inc. (TEC) comments – GVEC incorporates

by reference the comments of TEC, including concerns about applicability thresholds, curtailment

authority, CIAC treatment for cooperatives and MOUs, rate base offsets, financial security

requirements, study responsibility boundaries, and the need for additional comment opportunity if

the rule changes materially.
